record.paper_title: Twenty Open Problems in Enumeration of Matchings: Progress Report
record.context_brief: Parity of perfect matchings in the n-cube
record.original_question: For each positive integer n, does the number of perfect matchings of the n-dimensional cube have the same parity as n?

evidence.quote: Problem 19: Laszlo Lovasz gave a simple proof of my (oral) conjecture that the number of perfect matchings of the n-cube has the same parity as n itself.

artifact.self_contained_problem: For a positive integer $n$, let $Q_n$ denote the $n$-dimensional hypercube graph: its vertex set is $\{0,1\}^n$, and two vertices are adjacent if and only if they differ in exactly one coordinate. A perfect matching of $Q_n$ is a set of edges such that every vertex of $Q_n$ is incident to exactly one edge of the set. Let $m(n)$ denote the number of perfect matchings of $Q_n$. Prove or disprove: for every positive integer $n$, $m(n) \equiv n \pmod{2}$.
artifact.status_search_result: The problem has been resolved affirmatively: a short proof by L. Lovász establishes that the number of perfect matchings of the $n$-cube has the same parity as $n$.
